subject: Eval brief: recommended model shortlist & next milestones
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy@brightlinehealth.com>, Theo Ramos <theo.ramos@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Eval brief: recommended model shortlist & next milestones

Hi Amy / Theo —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the recommended next steps to get you to a 4-week PoC. I focused this note on model fit and practical tradeoffs so you can pick the route that matches Brightline's latency and hallucination tolerance.

High-level takeaways from the demo:
- Your primary workload: conversational triage and clinical-summaries extraction (avg user turn ~26 tokens, downstream QA on summaries).
- Key constraints: 95th-percentile latency target <= 450ms, hallucination tolerance is low for clinical summaries, throughput moderate (~300 requests/min).

Recommended shortlist (ranked by our recommendation order):
1) redwood-ft-13b-quant (balanced) — Quality: High for extraction tasks, hallucination moderate-to-low with prompt-set v1; p95 latency ~420ms on our dedicated profile; estimated cost ~ $75 / 1M tokens. Good default for production where accuracy matters.
2) open-7b-llamaq (low-latency / cost) — Quality: Good for routing/classification and short replies; p95 latency ~260ms; cost ~ $22 / 1M tokens. Higher chance of subtle omissions on longer summaries.
3) redwood-34b-int8 (quality-first) — Quality: Highest on benchmarks we ran (QA F1 + ROUGE), hallucination lowest; p95 latency ~900ms on equivalent infra (can be improved with dedicated capacity); cost ~ $320 / 1M tokens. Best where accuracy is non-negotiable and you can accept higher tail latency or pay for dedicated.

Why these three: they span the cost/latency/quality frontier for the workflows you described. We ran the Brightline prompt-set (link below) plus a 500-sample evaluation that includes factuality checks and summary QA. See attached eval_results_summary.csv for top-level numbers.

Short-term proposal (next milestones):
- Confirm your evaluation priority (A: minimize hallucination; B: minimize latency/cost; C: balanced).
- Redwood provides a 4-week PoC with a canary rollout plan: week 0–1 integration + metrics, week 2 controlled production traffic (10–20%), week 3 quality ramp, week 4 handoff & ops runbook.
- Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60m session with our SRE + solutions engineer to finalize p95 SLOs, caching, and KV/long-context handling.

Links / artifacts:
- Benchmarks & raw results: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/Brightline-0427
- Prompt set (v1): https://drive.redwood.com/prompts/brightline-promptset-v1
- Eval CSV (attached): eval_results_summary.csv

Immediate asks for Brightline:
1) Which evaluation priority (A / B / C) should we use?
2) Please confirm the security contact & procurement lead so we can share contracts and a targeted PO estimate.

I'll loop in Marissa for procurement & Karthik for the deeper model tradeoff questions. Happy to adjust the shortlist if you'd like different size/cost points.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Eval brief: recommended model shortlist & next milestones

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. Quick clarifications before we pick A/B/C: 

- On hallucination: can you call out typical failure modes you saw in the CSV for redwood-ft-13b-quant vs redwood-34b-int8? We need concrete examples for our clinical review board.
- Latency: our platform requires p95 <= 450ms for patient-facing flows; p95 <= 900ms is acceptable for internal batch-summary jobs. Can your balanced option hit the <450ms target consistently on a dedicated pool?
- Security: attaching our initial security questionnaire (security_questionnaire.pdf). We also need an estimate of data retention controls and KMS integration timeline.

Also looping in our CTO (Theo) — he'll want a quick line on procurement/PO cadence. We can commit to a 4-week PoC if we can get a concise SOW and cost estimate up front.

— Amy
Amy Park
Head of Product, Brightline Health
amy@brightlinehealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy@brightlinehealth.com>, Theo Ramos <theo.ramos@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval brief: recommended model shortlist & next milestones

Amy — thanks, good questions. Short answers + attachments/links below.

1) Failure-mode examples (from attached CSV):
- redwood-ft-13b-quant: occasionally omits secondary diagnoses in length >120 token summaries (~3% of samples). Most failures are omission, not hallucination. Example in CSV row 134 shows missing comorbidity; model produced concise but incomplete extraction.
- redwood-34b-int8: produces the most complete summaries; hallucination rate <0.5% on our factuality checks, but is sensitive to prompt phrasing (we include defensive prompt templates in the prompt-set).

2) Latency guarantees:
- Balanced profile (redwood-ft-13b-quant) can meet p95 <=450ms on dedicated capacity sized ~2x your observed concurrency. On hosted/shared infra p95 can spike; we recommend Reserved / Dedicated for production. We'll include a sizing recommendation in the PO estimate.

3) Security & retention:
- Redwood Private / Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and configurable retention windows. Typical KMS integration takes 2–5 business days with vendor test keys; we'll include a short checklist in the SOW.

Attached: po_cost_estimate.xlsx (high-level pricing for 4-week PoC + 6-month projection). I also linked the prompt-set and the benchmark CSV.

Operational mitigations for quality regression:
- Canary + shadowing: route a small % to candidate model and keep golden-model comparisons for automated alerts.
- Prompt regression tests: run your clinical test-suite on every model deploy; Redwood Optimize can run those continuous checks and fire regression alerts.
- Fallback policy: if quality or latency breaches, automatic routing to the nominated fallback (e.g., open-7b-llamaq for latency, redwood-34b-int8 for accuracy).

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan / Marissa to share SOW + formal PO estimate by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule technical deep-dive (we added Neha from Solutions; she can take the lead on the integration plan).

If you want, I can produce a short 2-slide decision memo comparing the three models (cost / latency / quality) for your CTO.

— Jordan

Action items I'll drive:
- Draft SOW & PO estimate (based on po_cost_estimate.xlsx) and share to Amy/Theo by EOD tomorrow.
- Coordinate KMS checklist with Brightline security team (Neha, I'll need the contact in the questionnaire).
- Book technical deep-dive with Karthik & Neha (45–60m) for Tue/Wed next week — Karthik, can you share availability?

Thanks — Marissa
